title: A toy word chooser
summary: A language model predicts possible next pieces of text. This tiny list only illustrates choosing a next word; it is not a trained language model.
introduction: A language model predicts possible next pieces of text. This tiny list only illustrates choosing a next word; it is not a trained language model. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A language model predicts possible next pieces of text. This tiny list only illustrates choosing a next word; it is not a trained language model.

blocks.code:
choices = [("flies", 6), ("rests", 3), ("sings", 1)]
word = max(choices, key=lambda item: item[1])[0]
print("The kite", word)
blocks.title: A toy word chooser

blocks.text: The output is The kite flies. max finds the pair with the largest hand-written score. [0] then selects its word.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the score for rests to 7 and predict the result.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Hand-written scores in a list do not recreate how a large model learns language.
